title: Product Designer
description:
In the 1960s, the Italian artist and inventor Bruno Munari was studying spontaneous forms: shapes that emerge from the interaction of material, function, and environment.

When Danese Milano commissioned him to design a lamp that was practical, durable, affordable, and easy to transport, Munari was reminded of the traditional rice paper lanterns he had encountered when traveling in Japan. But rice paper lanterns are fragile, hard to clean, and tend to yellow over time.

Looking for an industrial alternative, he discovered filanca—a synthetic stretch nylon used exclusively for women's stockings at the time.

Munari visited hosiery factories to test the material and see what forms it could take. "We do not make lamps, sir. Only stockings," one factory told him. Munari replied, "You'll see."

The result was the Falkland lamp: only a few centimeters thick when packaged, as tall as a human when hung, its spontaneous form emerging from the elasticity of the nylon and metal rings of different diameters inserted at regular intervals, enlarged by gravity when suspended from above.

Munari didn't begin with the form of a lamp. He began with the qualities it needed, then looked outside the conventions of lighting to find the right materials and methods. We're looking for a designer who works the same way: someone who studies the systems and materials at hand, then finds a way of putting them together that feels both unexpected and inevitable.

At Co–Star, the materials are a 4,000-year-old system of astrology, planetary data from NASA, and a corpus written by astrologers and poets. The qualities we're designing for: astrology made accessible without asking anyone to learn a complex system, and a language that lets people share something intimate with their friends.

We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to continue cultivating those qualities across Co–Star and new experiments. You'll move between product architecture, interaction design, prototyping, and visual design. Ideas rarely arrive as polished specs. You'll help decide what we make next and how it works.

What you'll do



- Design and build products from concept through launch.
- Work closely with design and engineering on new features and launches.
- You care about the details—typography, layout, motion, responsiveness, loading states, and performance—that make an experience great.
- Contribute visual assets for marketing.
- Prototype ideas quickly using Figma, Claude, Cursor, and whatever tools helps move the work forward.

You might be a fit if



- You have 2–5 years of experience designing and building for the web.
- You move fluidly across the full design process, from early concept through final production.
- You have an instinct for the details that make interfaces feel considered: type, spacing, motion, and how they all work together.
- You know enough HTML and CSS to work effectively with engineers—or to build parts of the experience yourself.
- You're comfortable using tools like Claude

description:
About Us

At Roadrunner, we’re replacing the broken CPQ software that Sales teams have complained about, worked around, and given up on for years. Not improving it - replacing it. We’re building a new agentic stack called PQA - Prompt, Quote, Approve, designed for the enterprise, on a data model built for how pricing actually works today.

We’re Kleiner Perkins’ first incubation since Glean, led by second-time founders with successful exits, and a team of engineers from Snowflake, Databricks, Citadel, Meta, Robinhood, Brex, and so on. We’re in-person in San Francisco, and we’re just getting started.

What You’ll Do



- Set the tone for how the product looks and feels. You'll curate the taste of the product — every interaction, layout, and detail should feel intentional. 
- Turn hard problems into UI that just works. CPQ is full of complex workflows and dense data — you'll make them feel simple without hiding the complexity users actually need. 
- Work directly with engineers and the people using what you build. You'll be embedded with engineers on dedicated workstreams, making decisions in real time. Get feedback fast, iterate faster. 
- Design with AI tools, for AI-native workflows. You'll shape how users interact with and trust AI agents, and use AI in your own process to move fast. 
- Build an airtight design system. You'll evolve our design system so you and engineers can ship consistent UI at speed. 

Example projects



- Designing a quoting experience that lets AEs configure complex multi-product deals in minutes instead of hours. 
- Defining the visual language and component patterns for approval workflows that handle multibillion-dollar transactions — where clarity isn't a nice-to-have, it's a requirement. 
- Evolving our design system to support new product surfaces while keeping the token architecture clean and the component library tight. 

What You’ll Bring



- Systems thinking. You see patterns across screens and build for reuse, not one-offs. 
- High autonomy and a builder's mindset — you figure out what needs to be designed and do it. 
- Experience designing with AI tools to move faster without sacrificing quality. 
- Clear, direct communication with engineers and founders. You can articulate why a design works, not just what it looks like. 
- Based in SF or excited to relocate — we're an in-person team. 

Bonus points if…



- Strong visual chops — you sweat the details on layout, typography, color, and spacing

What Lumion does
Lumion is the all-in-one operating system for trade and technical schools. We power the entire institution: AI-driven lead generation and conversion, enrollment, financial aid, student lifecycle management, and tuition payments. Most schools are still stitching together five or six disconnected tools to do what our platform handles.


America has a massive skilled trades shortage and the schools that train electricians, welders, and nurses are the bottleneck. We're backed by TTV Capital and Tusk Venture Partners.
Why this role matters


You would be Lumion's first dedicated product designer. Until now, design has been done by the founders, product managers, and engineers. That carried us a long way, and it is no longer enough.


Our engineers build with AI-native workflows, so the constraint on the product is no longer how fast we can write code. It is how fast we can figure out exactly what to build and make it excellent. That is design work, and right now it is our bottleneck.


The people who use our platform are admissions directors, school owners, and finance staff who live in it all day, and students making one of the bigger financial decisions of their lives. Most software in this industry was built a decade ago and looks like it. You get to set the bar for what great looks like in this market.


The work
You will own design across the entire platform.


Product design end to end. You take features from PRD to shipped: user flows, interaction design, high-fidelity UI, and specs engineers can build from without guessing. You will work directly with the CEO and CTO in design sessions and own the outcome.


Prototypes. Before engineering commits to a build, we want a working prototype in front of real schools. You will produce clickable, testable prototypes fast and use what you learn to sharpen the spec before a line of production code gets written.


The design system. The platform spans lead management, enrollment, messaging, scheduling, payments, and reporting, and it grew fast. You will build the component library and interaction patterns that make it feel like one product, and that let engineers ship good UI without a designer in the room.


AI interfaces. Schools use Lumion to configure and supervise AI agents that text, email, and call prospective students. Designing how a non-technical admissions director sets up an agent, reviews its conversations, and learns to trust it is new territory with little prior art. You will define those patterns.


Student surfaces. Enrollment applications, document signing, and tuition payments, mostly on a phone. These flows handle real money and real decisions, and they have to be effortless.

With a strong foundation in UI/UX design, you bring a true product mindset to your work. You look beyond the pixels to deeply understand business goals, technical constraints, and user outcomes. You do not just ask how a feature should look; you ask how it drives value, how to measure success, and how it impacts the broader ecosystem. You enjoy the unique challenge of enterprise and data-heavy applications, taking pride in turning complex requirements into clear, usable, and intuitive workflows.

You take great pride in your craft, but you view your first drafts as collaborative starting points rather than precious artifacts. You welcome constructive feedback as a powerful tool for improvement and are eager to learn alongside a team of seasoned experts. Additionally, you see AI as a true partner in the design process. You regularly leverage modern tools to accelerate your research, explore a wider range of design variations, and automate repetitive tasks, allowing you to dedicate your focus to high-level problem-solving.

- Minimum of two to four years of professional experience in UI/UX design

- A sharp eye for typography, hierarchy, and layout defines your foundational craft

The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. Until now.

description:
About ONO
At ONO, we design sleek, silent tools that help busy minds find a moment of clarity. Our flagship, the patented ONO Roller, is in the hands of more than 500,000 people worldwide, from overwhelmed students to design-obsessed professionals looking for a quieter way to focus.
We are a small, purpose-driven team that believes tactile tools can quietly support mental wellbeing. We move fast, execute with intent, and obsess over the details that make a product worth holding.


The Role
We are hiring a Junior Industrial Designer to help design the next generation of ONO products. You will work directly with our founder and own real deliverables, from first sketch to something we can put in front of a manufacturer. This is hands-on product design for someone who loves physical objects and understands what makes them tick: the click of a mechanism, the weight in your palm, the feel of a good detent.


This is an ongoing part-time, hourly role. We are looking for a designer who wants steady, flexible part-time work designing products that ship. Hours generally run 10 to 30 per week depending on what is in the pipeline.


You will get a Fusion 360 license and a direct line to the founder. You bring the portfolio, the modeling chops, and the instinct for how a product should function.


What You'll Own
Product Design & Development

- Design new fidget concepts, from rough sketches through refined, manufacturable 3D models.
- Model and iterate in Fusion 360, thinking through mechanisms, tolerances, and materials.
- Apply light engineering judgment so products feel right in the hand and hold up in production.
- Prototype, test, and refine based on how the object actually performs.
Packaging Design

- Design packaging that feels as considered as the product inside it.
- Prepare files and specs to hand off to print and manufacturing partners.
Trade Show & Physical Brand Presence

- Design our trade show booth and physical presence for events.
- Translate the ONO look into physical spaces, displays, and fixtures.
Graphic Design (as needed)

- Create graphic assets across product, packaging, and brand as projects require.
Concept Communication

- Present and communicate concepts clearly through sketches, renders, and short decks.
- Walk the founder and partners through your thinking so decisions move quickly.


What You Bring

- Portfolio: physical product design work, ideally toys, gadgets, or everyday-carry objects, showing both form and function.
- Fusion 360: working proficiency, including modeling for manufacture.
- Product instinct: a real feel for how things work, not just how they look.
- Sketching: strong hand skills and the ability to explain ideas visually.
- Communication: comfort presenting concepts and talking through tradeoffs.

We are seeking a Product Designer II to create exceptional user experiences across FOX News Media's digital products, including FOX News, FOX Business and OutKick. You'll design intuitive, engaging experiences across multiple product teams, contributing strong UI/UX craft to initiatives ranging from content discovery and audience engagement to emerging AI-powered experiences.

In this role, you'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, and fellow designers to solve user problems, translate requirements into thoughtful designs, and deliver high-quality web and mobile experiences. You'll have opportunities to grow your product thinking while contributing across the full design process—from discovery and ideation through implementation.

You'll iterate in a fast-paced, collaborative environment where priorities evolve quickly, experimentation is encouraged, and AI-powered tools help accelerate design and prototyping.

A SNAPSHOT OF YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

 Product Design 



-  Design user experiences across web and mobile products, contributing from concept through implementation. 
-  Support translation of user needs, product requirements, and business goals into intuitive, user-centered experiences. 
-  Create user flows, wireframes, high-fidelity mockups, and interactive prototypes that clearly communicate design intent. 
-  Apply user-centered design principles while balancing usability, technical feasibility, and business objectives.

-  Produce polished, visually engaging designs that align with FOX News Media's brand and accessibility standards. 
-  Apply strong visual design fundamentals, including typography, hierarchy, layout, color, and interaction design. 
-  Contribute to design systems and reusable components to promote consistency across products. 
-  Support collaboration with Engineering throughout implementation to ensure design quality and accuracy. 

 AI-Driven Design & Prototyping 



-  Develop and apply fluency in AI tools ( Figma AI, Claude Design, or similar) to accelerate ideation, visual exploration, and concepting. 
-  Build functional prototypes that help communicate concepts and validate user experiences. 
-  Apply general-purpose AI assistants (Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, or similar) for research synthesis, UX copy, and design brief development. 
-  Stay current on emerging AI-powered design tools and seek opportunities to incorporate them into day-to-day workflows.

title: Visual Designer, Product
description:
You'll own the visual quality of Luma's product: the typography, color, iconography, spacing, and components that make it feel exceptional, and the design system that lets the whole team hold that bar as the product grows. This is a craft-first role with a strong point of view.

It isn't a redesign-everything role. You're elevating what exists and building the scalable foundation underneath it, including a living design system engineers and designers actually reference when they build. It fits someone who thinks in systems and can defend why a decision is right, not just how it looks. If you prefer one-off screens over a coherent system, this won't suit.

title: Founding Product Designer
description:
About Ceno

Ceno is building the neobank for the US-to-Asia corridor: one account where Americans invest in global equities, hold and move USD, KRW, and JPY, and run a financial life that spans two continents.

We're starting with the hardest and most valuable piece: a retail brokerage that gives US investors direct access to Korean and Japanese equities. USD in, USD out, with FX, custody, KYC, and tax reporting handled invisibly by an AI-native, agentic back end. Recent regulatory changes in Korea opened direct market access to overseas brokers for the first time, and we intend to turn that opening into the default way America invests in Asia.

The product promise is true localization: buying any global equity feels exactly like trading the US markets, with the research, filings, and news that local investors trade on translated and delivered in real time by our AI research engine. From there the map expands, market by market, until global equities sit on one shelf, with stablecoin-enabled settlement moving money across the Pacific in minutes instead of days. The AAPI community is our beachhead; US retail is the market.

We're seed-stage, on a multi-phase path to our own FINRA-licensed broker-dealer, and building the founding team now. There is no design team yet. You are it.

Why this role exists

A brokerage is its interface. In a category no one has seen before, buying a Korean or Japanese stock, the design is the product: it is what makes an unfamiliar, intimidating action feel as ordinary as buying Apple. Robinhood proved that design can create a category; Coinbase proved that design is what earns trust when people move real money into something they don't fully understand. Ceno needs both, and it needs them from the first screen.

This is a founding-team seat with full ownership of product design end to end: the mobile app, the onboarding and funding flows, the trading and research surfaces, the design system, and the brand as it shows up in the product. You are the first designer, so you both set the vision and push the pixels. You'll partner directly with the CEO on what we build, with the CTO and engineers on how it ships, and with the growth team on how it converts. Three things define the first 12 months.



- Onboarding to a funded account. Design the flow that turns a curious download into a KYC-verified, funded, trading account. This is the number the company lives on, and it runs straight through your screens: sign-up, identity, funding, first trade.
- Making the foreign feel native. Design a trading and research experience where a Korean or Japanese equity, its price, its filings, its news, its currency, feels as legible and safe as a US stock. This is the core product bet, and it is fundamentally a design problem.
- The system and the bar. Establish Ceno's design language and component system from zero, and set a quality bar high enough that a regulated financial product feels trustworthy and a consumer product feels delightful,

title: Founding Product Designer
description:
About Ceno

Ceno is building the neobank for the US-to-Asia corridor: one account where Americans invest in global equities, hold and move USD, KRW, and JPY, and run a financial life that spans two continents.

We're starting with the hardest and most valuable piece: a retail brokerage that gives US investors direct access to Korean and Japanese equities. USD in, USD out, with FX, custody, KYC, and tax reporting handled invisibly by an AI-native, agentic back end. Recent regulatory changes in Korea opened direct market access to overseas brokers for the first time, and we intend to turn that opening into the default way America invests in Asia.

The product promise is true localization: buying any global equity feels exactly like trading the US markets, with the research, filings, and news that local investors trade on translated and delivered in real time by our AI research engine. From there the map expands, market by market, until global equities sit on one shelf, with stablecoin-enabled settlement moving money across the Pacific in minutes instead of days. The AAPI community is our beachhead; US retail is the market.

We're seed-stage, on a multi-phase path to our own FINRA-licensed broker-dealer, and building the founding team now. There is no design team yet. You are it.

Why this role exists

A brokerage is its interface. In a category no one has seen before, buying a Korean or Japanese stock, the design is the product: it is what makes an unfamiliar, intimidating action feel as ordinary as buying Apple. Robinhood proved that design can create a category; Coinbase proved that design is what earns trust when people move real money into something they don't fully understand. Ceno needs both, and it needs them from the first screen.

This is a founding-team seat with full ownership of product design end to end: the mobile app, the onboarding and funding flows, the trading and research surfaces, the design system, and the brand as it shows up in the product. You are the first designer, so you both set the vision and push the pixels. You'll partner directly with the CEO on what we build, with the CTO and engineers on how it ships, and with the growth team on how it converts. Three things define the first 12 months.



- Onboarding to a funded account. Design the flow that turns a curious download into a KYC-verified, funded, trading account. This is the number the company lives on, and it runs straight through your screens: sign-up, identity, funding, first trade.
- Making the foreign feel native. Design a trading and research experience where a Korean or Japanese equity, its price, its filings, its news, its currency, feels as legible and safe as a US stock. This is the core product bet, and it is fundamentally a design problem.
- The system and the bar. Establish Ceno's design language and component system from zero, and set a quality bar high enough that a regulated financial product feels trustworthy and a consumer product feels delightful,

title: Principal Product Designer
description:
About Agora Intelligence (d.b.a. Tilt)
Agora Intelligence is building the audited methodology layer agents call before touching portfolios. Our product, Tilt, is GitHub for rules-based investment methodologies: an open platform and marketplace where investment strategies are created, tested, audited, and distributed — by humans and AI agents alike. As AI agents begin managing real portfolios, they need a trusted source of verified investment logic before they can act. Tilt is that source.
We operate across two connected surfaces: InvestOS, an open standard that lets any brokerage or platform plug verified methodology into its own AI experience; and Tilt, the reference implementation of InvestOS. Tilt is an agentic harness where investors, portfolio managers, and creators can author, remix, and publish strategies. We're a small, senior team (from BlackRock, Bloomberg, BGI, and Quant Funds) backed by Portage Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Cumberland Investments (and more), working with major brokerages and financial data providers.


What We're Building
InvestOS — an open standard for rules-based methodologies and its reference implementation.
We believe any idea — a theme, a trend, a thesis — can be turned into an investable view. On Tilt, anyone can express a view as a rules-based basket of assets in seconds, backed by evidence and scored against what actually happens. Whether you're modeling a thematic strategy, tracking an emerging technology, or capturing the public-market footprint of a private company, what used to take an index committee months now takes an API call — 100× faster, at a fraction of the cost. We also transform views found on the open web, into rules-based strategies. This lets us measure the performance of any opinion or prediction about the future. The unit is a tilt: a creator-authored view of the world.


The bigger bet: as AI agents take on more of investing, they'll need an open, trusted standard for how investment views are expressed, verified, and combined. When anyone can generate a strategy in seconds, the strategies aren't the asset. The system that versions, tests, and grades them is. We're building that standard — and the platform where those views are made. We’re also building the learning loops for when views resolve against reality, as measured by markets.


Who We Are
We're a team of ~25 senior-to-principal engineers, designers and AI/ML researchers. More than half the team are former founders. We move fast, challenge assumptions, and believe AI should fundamentally change how financial products are built. We have no management hierarchy and work remotely with 4 one-week hackathons per year. “Full stack” to us means you own a slice of the product, including its roadmap and go-to-market.

About Us

Our mission is to reinvent the way people learn, starting with language.

Learning a language can change a life by opening doors to new cultures, careers, and communities. Two billion people around the world are actively trying to learn a language, but the best way to learn (one-on-one tutoring) is hard to access at scale and hasn’t been meaningfully improved in decades. Speak is building a human-level, AI-powered tutor in your pocket: a conversation-first experience that lets learners actually speak, get instant feedback, and progress through carefully designed lessons. The result is a complete path from beginner to confident speaker across multiple languages.

Speak first launched in South Korea in 2019, where Speak has now become the number one language learning app, and we now serve learners across many markets and 15+ languages. Speak is one of the world’s leading AI companies, with over $150m raised in venture investment from OpenAI, Accel, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and more, with a distributed team across San Francisco, Seoul, Tokyo, Taipei, and Ljubljana.

About The Design Team

We’re a small, high-craft team that sits at the intersection of research, invention, and product thinking. We build consumer and B2B experiences used by millions across 150+ markets — and a lot of the work is genuinely novel: inventing how someone talks to an AI tutor, what feedback feels like when you’re learning out loud, and how progress should be measured and celebrated.

We stay close to learners through prototyping, interviews, betas, and experiments. We take craft seriously, iterate fast, and value a high-trust critique-and-build culture. We have something to prove — and we care about doing work that is both useful and genuinely excellent.

About This Role

We’re hiring a seasoned Designer to improve how design and engineering work together, starting with a world-class, agent-first design system.

By agent-first, we mean the system is structured so humans and AI agents can make the same good decisions: choosing the right components, applying the right patterns, using consistent names, and reviewing UI against shared rules.

This is a systems thinker, high-craft, high-collaboration role. You’ll work closely with dedicated engineers who will be your collaborators in bringing this to life across our product surfaces. description:
IFS is a billion-dollar revenue company with 7000+ employees on all continents. We deliver award-winning enterprise software solutions through the use of embedded digital innovation and a single cloud-based platform to help businesses be their best when it really matters–at the Moment of Service™.


At IFS, we're flexible, we're innovative, and we're focused not only on how we can engage with our customers, but on how we can make a real change and have a worldwide impact. By joining our team, you will have the opportunity to be part of a global, diverse environment; you will be joining a winning team with a commitment to sustainability; and a company where we get things done so that you can make a positive impact on the world.


We're looking for innovative and original thinkers to work in an environment where you can #MakeYourMoment so that we can help others make theirs.


If you want to change the status quo, we'll help you make your moment. Join Team Purple. Join IFS.



Job Description


You'll be designing for people whose work actually matters: maintenance engineers, field service technicians, operations planners working in environments where the software either helps or gets in the way. The stakes are real and the problems are hard, which is exactly what makes this role interesting.


At IFS, product design means owning the full problem, not just the screens. You'll work in a cross-functional squad alongside engineers and product managers, with the scope and support to do the work properly. From problem framing through to something shipped and measured.

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
About Nuvo

Nuvo is building the infrastructure that powers trade in the physical goods economy.

Every part of modern life depends on physical goods: the food we eat, the fabric we wear, the steel and concrete that shape our cities. Behind it all are 50 million businesses trading $100 trillion each year.

Consider how housing gets built. One company cuts down trees, another turns the wood into building materials, another sells the product wholesale, and a contractor uses them to build homes. Each step is a business trading with another to turn raw materials into finished goods.

Most of these businesses still operate through offline networks, held together by fragmented systems, manual processes, and institutional memory. When trade is slow, costly, or error-prone, the effects cascade — resources get misallocated, businesses can’t grow, and consumers face higher costs and fewer choices.

Nuvo builds technology that makes trade fast, automated, and intelligent. More than 75,000 businesses already use our platform, and we’re backed by $45M from Sequoia, Spark, Founders Fund, and Index as we build the operating system for global commerce.

The Role

Design at Nuvo sits at the center of how our platform works and feels. Our products span identity, risk, payments, AI, and more, all built on top of the connectivity between businesses on our platform. As a Senior Product Designer, you’ll shape how this system comes to life for thousands of businesses, defining how complex operations become simple, intuitive, and powerful.

You’ll operate with deep ownership, collaborating closely with engineering, product, and customer teams. You’ll help define the next generation of experiences that make Nuvo increasingly compelling across new industries and use cases.

What You’ll Do



- Drive design for major product areas that serve thousands of businesses

- Help define the design team’s culture, identity, and creative standards

Who You Are



- You gain deep context to set a high standard for what gets built, how, and why
- You learn quickly, connect patterns across identity, payments, and data, and use that understanding to shape product direction
- You collaborate with engineers, PMs, and other stakeholders, making thoughtful trade-offs, relaying context, and being a clear voice of the customer
- Have 5+ years in industry shipping high-impact products to solve complex problems

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
Description

Position at Everyday Health - Consumer

The Opportunity

Everyday Health Group is looking for a Senior Product Designer who thinks in systems, not screens.

This role supports design across Everyday Health Group's portfolio of consumer brands. You'll be working across distinct audiences and business models under one roof, from health and wellness content to lifestyle and subscription products, with the mix of brands and depth of involvement shifting over time. That range is part of the job.

AI has changed what this job is. Wireframes, first-draft flows, and visual options that used to take days now take minutes. That's not a threat to this role, it's the reason this role exists. We need designers who use AI to clear the production work off their plate so they can spend their time on the part AI can't do: framing the right problem, making the hard call between two defensible options, and understanding why a user actually behaves the way they do.

This isn't just a shipping role. We want someone who brings a point of view on where a brand or product should go next, not just how to execute what's already been scoped.

If you're looking for a job where you produce assets on request, this isn't it. If you want a job where your judgment is the product, keep reading.

Key Responsibilities



- Own design across Everyday Health Group's portfolio of consumer brands, with varying depth across brands, from problem framing through shipped experience
- Explore multiple directions for a problem before committing, including options outside the current roadmap or sprint, and bring a point of view on where a brand or product should go next
- Use AI tools to generate options and prototype fast, then apply editorial judgment to decide what actually ships
- Use AI tools to analyze user testing sessions and surface patterns, applying judgment to determine what the findings actually mean for the design
- Use AI tools to accelerate early-stage research (requirements gathering, competitive analysis, stakeholder feedback synthesis), then apply judgment to decide what's worth acting on
- Design solutions that hold up across devices and breakpoints, with a mobile-first mindset
- Translate business goals ("improve retention," "reduce drop-off") into specific, testable design questions
- Partner directly with Product, Engineering, Editorial, Analytics, and Sales/Ad Ops to frame problems before jumping to solutions
- Think in systems: understand how a change to one flow ripples across the rest of the product, including edge cases and downstream platforms
- Present design rationale to stakeholders at every level, from engineers to senior leadership, in language each audience actually finds useful
- Advocate for the user in rooms where the user isn't represented, including flagging when a feature's promise and its actual impact don't line up
- Contribute to and help evolve our design systems, keeping consistency without slowing down iteration
- Maintain and extend

Strategic sequencing. Cheap experiments must compound into defensible architecture, not pile up as disconnected features.

About Us

About The Role

Hey 👋 Kyle here. I run product and growth at Conversion, and up until now I've also been the person holding our brand. Every logo lockup, every deck, every launch page, every color and type call. I've loved doing it. It's also the thing I most need to hand off, and the hardest for me to let go of.

So, now I'm hiring a brand designer. Someone who owns our visual identity top to bottom and builds the system the rest of the company designs against.

That means you're the person who decides what Conversion looks like and feels like everywhere it shows up. The identity system (logo, type, color, grid, motion language), the guidelines that keep it consistent, and the craft bar that everything gets held to. You'll bring it to life across web, social, launch creative, decks, and collateral. When we ship a new feature or run a launch, you're making the page look incredible, cutting the launch video, and setting the visual story. This is brand and identity work, not product UI (Levi owns our in-app surfaces), and not code. If you think of yourself as a design engineer, this probably isn't your seat.

I care about this a lot, which is why the bar is high. Portfolio first, always. I want to see identity work you've built from the ground up and can walk me through: what the problem was, what you made, why every decision. I'd rather see one brand you shaped end to end than ten logos you touched. Tool fluency is table stakes (Figma, Illustrator, After Effects / Lottie / Figma Motion, Claude Design), and I'm looking for roughly 1 to 5 years of doing exactly this.

The people who crush this role tend to be the same off the clock. Side projects, an art Instagram, a vlog, a brand they built just because. Strong opinions about advertising and what good creative actually is (I keep a Super Bowl ad tier list, so no judgment). The friend whose dinner party has a custom menu. Obsessive about craft down to the pixel. If that's you, and you want to own a brand rather than execute someone else's, this is a rare one.

This role is in-person 5 days/week in San Francisco.

What You'll Own



- The visual identity itself: logo, type, color, grid, motion language, and the guidelines that keep all of it consistent as more people build on top of it
- The look and feel of Conversion everywhere it shows up: web, social, decks, collateral, launch creative
- Launch work end to end: the launch

description:
About Auxilius
Auxilius builds clinical trial financial management software that helps drug companies take control over trial costs, manage financial risk, and optimize R&D spend. We provide data, context, and frameworks that empower teams to bring drugs to market faster and more cost-effectively.
With 100+ customers relying on our platform today, we're at an exciting inflection point where thoughtful product decisions have real impact, and the ability to quickly translate customer needs into intuitive scalable solutions can unlock massive market opportunity.


The Role
We're looking for a Product Manager to own the data moat end to end: how external data gets into Auxilius, how we model and connect it once it's in, and how users query it and act on it.
Auxilius wins on data. The more sources we connect and the better we model what lands, the more we can do for sponsors that no one else can. You'll work across three pillars: Integrations, Data Platform, and Activation + AI, and you'll be expected to move fluidly between driving our integration roadmap, partnering on our data warehouse, and shaping how AI features surface value back to users.


Why This Matters
The life sciences industry spends $250-300 billion annually on clinical R&D, yet outcomes remain stubbornly poor. Even when the science works—when the data shows promise—trials rarely finish on time or on budget. The cost of drug development has risen relentlessly for decades (Eroom's Law), and the industry has accepted this as inevitable.
We don't.
At Auxilius, we believe science matters, but trial outcomes depend on more than science alone. We believe sponsors deserve tools built to handle the complexity of clinical trials, and that while science is inherently unpredictable, budgets don't need to be. We're building software that proves biotechs can bring drugs to market quickly and cost-effectively—it just takes the right tools.
This is your chance to own the data foundation the rest of the company builds on, at a stage where what you build will define the company—and help reshape an entire industry's approach to R&D efficiency.

- Communicate timelines and manage work stream directly with Sponsor’s IT and technical teams as part of initial integration build during customer implementation

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
About PactFi

Private asset markets (PE, Private Credit, VC, Real Estate) have 10x to 9.8T in AUM over the past decade and are projected to grow to $17T in the next five years. However, digital infrastructure has not kept pace, with most of the market operating predominantly in error-prone, internal-only software solutions.

PactFi provides secure, end-to-end, operational infrastructure for managing complex private credit transactions. Our web-based application brings together all parties involved in such a transaction to more efficiently allocate capital, complete KYC, share documents, manage funds flow, and more. The platform is secured to a bank-grade standard, and we have received our SOC 2 Type 2 attestation.

PactFi was developed in close partnership with two of the industry's largest players, both of whom represent the top 3 players in the private credit space by both size (AUM) and deal activity.

The Design Problem



- Product is moving from a screen-first build model, where the underlying system is designed first and the interface follows. 
- Today's product is fully deterministic, human-driven screens. You'd help define, from scratch, what this platform looks like as AI becomes a first-class part of it — AI agents as a new type of participant alongside human users, and AI as a new interaction modality for human users themselves. 
- Workflows are tied to assets that can live 5–7 years, resurfacing repeatedly at different cadences over that lifetime, with multiple parties holding different views and permissions each time. 
- Clients regularly bring new deal and asset structures the platform hasn't seen before, so the product has to accommodate structural variation it can't fully anticipate. 
- Permissioning is layered — participants often have their own downstream stakeholders who need visibility into a subset of the same information. 
- A point of view on how AI is reshaping what a "product" is — where a great interface is still needed versus where the underlying data itself, exposed well, is becoming the product — is a plus. 

What You'll Do



- Own one or two major product surfaces end-to-end — from problem framing through shipped, polished detail. 
- Design and ship the platform's first real AI-native interaction pattern in an otherwise fully deterministic product — no existing pattern to extend from. 
- Design for dense, structured financial data at scale, and for multi-party, long-running workflows with layered permissions. 
- Work closely with the PM and engineers on your surface to develop the strategy and rationale behind what you build, not just execute a spec. 
- Contribute to and help shape a design system built for extensibility across evolving workflows and asset structures. 
- Set an example in critique and day-to-day work for how design is done here — the work itself is the signal, not a title or mandate.

Our focus is on building the platform that helps restaurants adapt, take control, and get back to what they do best: building the businesses they love. And because our technology is purpose-built for restaurants, by restaurant people, restaurants can trust that we'll deliver on their needs for today while investing in experiences that will power their restaurant of the future. Toast IQ is our AI assistant, designed to give restaurant operators smarter insights, deeper personalization, and the ability to take action across the Toast ecosystem. We recently gave our brand an epic refresh, and now we're looking for someone who's excited to help shape what comes next. This isn't a role where you'll be handed a brand guide and told to color inside the lines. You'll help evolve the visual identity of one of the fastest-growing companies in the email marketing space, creating work that's memorable, clever and unmistakably Inbox Monster.
We're looking for someone based in Atlanta for a hybrid role, with 1–2 days a week in our Buckhead office for collaboration, creative brainstorming and the occasional excuse to eat tacos together.

What You'll Do


- Create bold, beautiful, on-brand creative across our website, landing pages, email campaigns, social media, presentations, print and whatever comes next.

- Partner closely with our Head of Marketing and Content Lead to dream up campaigns that stand out in crowded inboxes (and crowded LinkedIn feeds).
- Bring ideas to the table, not just pixels. We love designers who think strategically and bring big ideas to the whiteboard.

- A passion for great visual storytelling, thoughtful typography (we’re very protective of our custom Monstie Sans font) and clean, modern design.
- Incredible attention to detail and pride in your work. Good enough doesn’t exist in this role. 

Bonus Points If You Have


- Experience designing for a SaaS or technology company.
- Experience in email marketing (or an unhealthy fascination with it).
- Motion, illustration or light front-end skills that help bring your ideas to life.

About Inbox Monster

Inbox Monster helps email teams send with confidence. Inbox Monster’s deliverability and testing tools turn insights into action with complete visibility into email performance. Get proactive support that cares about your brand’s reputation as much as you do. Companies that trust Inbox Monster can save up to 53% of their time on QA and achieve a 30% improvement in inbox placement in 30 days. Find your email rawwwr at inboxmonster.com.

Dealerware transforms the automotive retailers of today into the mobility network of tomorrow. Launched in 2016, Dealerware manages tens of thousands of vehicles at dealerships in North America across every major manufacturer brand. Dealerware is committed to being a people-first culture and a great place to work for all, with flexible scheduling, unlimited PTO, extensive benefits, and a leadership team that defaults to being supportive and accessible. Digital experience is the connective tissue of Dealerware’s platform. Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

Our mission on the Developer Platform Team is to help game studios succeed by creating meaningful experiences for players. As a B2B2C team, we serve two key audiences. title: Freelance Brand Designer
description:
Remote · 3 to 4 week project · Start immediately


About ProMom
ProMom is an AI companion for the whole motherhood journey, from trying to conceive through pregnancy and postpartum. One app instead of six, with guidance shaped by a Medical Advisory Team of OB-GYNs and pediatricians. We are private by design, we do not sell user data, and we are ad free.


We are a small, fast team. Our users are often overwhelmed, anxious, and exhausted. Everything we build has to feel calm.


The project
We are mid-way through a full redesign of the app. Two in-house UX designers are building in Figma right now, and they are blocked on brand decisions. We need a brand designer to make those decisions and hand them a system they can build with immediately.


This is not a brand guide that gets delivered at the end and filed away. Your work goes straight into a live product build, week by week.


What you will deliver

- Color palette. A brand palette for marketing, plus an extended app color system that can express user stage (trying to conceive, pregnancy, postpartum) and functional states.
- Typography. Type direction for brand and app. Our current type reads techy. We want calm, human, and legible when someone is tired.
- Logo and app icon. A light refresh of the existing logo, evolution not redesign, plus the lockups we need. And a new App Store icon that reads at 60px on a home screen, our most-seen brand asset.
- Illustration style and brand design elements. The visual language that carries across app and marketing.
- Iconography direction. You set the style and our in-house UX team builds the library against it. If the icons only need a restyle, that is a direction-and-review job. If they need a full redesign, we will decide together who is best placed to build them.
- Brand style guide. Documented in Figma with our UX team as we go, so brand and app stay one system.
Not in scope: photography, marketing templates, website design.


How we work together
You lead brand direction and design judgment. Our two UX designers execute at scale. That means a kickoff together, a weekly working session, and shared Figma access so they can build with your work in real time rather than waiting.


Sequence matters. Color and typography come first because the app build is blocked on them. Illustration and icon direction follow immediately after, not at the end, because our designers are producing those assets now.


What we need from you
Must have

- Strong color, typography, and systems thinking. You have built a color and type system that shipped inside a real product, not just a logo and a moodboard.
- Experience across both brand and product design. You can hand a UX team something they can actually build with.
- Real availability. This is the single biggest factor for us. Roughly 12 to 20 hours a week for the next 3 to 4 weeks, starting now. If you are fitting this around a full-time job, it is probably not a fit.
- Free of any employer restriction on outside work a

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
In the 1960s, the Italian artist and inventor Bruno Munari was studying spontaneous forms: shapes that emerge from the interaction of material, function, and environment.

When Danese Milano commissioned him to design a lamp that was practical, durable, affordable, and easy to transport, Munari was reminded of the traditional rice paper lanterns he had encountered when traveling in Japan. But rice paper lanterns are fragile, hard to clean, and tend to yellow over time.

Looking for an industrial alternative, he discovered filanca—a synthetic stretch nylon used exclusively for women's stockings at the time.

Munari visited hosiery factories to test the material and see what forms it could take. "We do not make lamps, sir. Only stockings," one factory told him. Munari replied, "You'll see."

The result was the Falkland lamp: only a few centimeters thick when packaged, as tall as a human when hung, its spontaneous form emerging from the elasticity of the nylon and metal rings of different diameters inserted at regular intervals, enlarged by gravity when suspended from above.

Munari didn't begin with the form of a lamp. He began with the qualities it needed, then looked outside the conventions of lighting to find the right materials and methods. We're looking for a designer who works the same way: someone who studies the systems and materials at hand, then finds a way of putting them together that feels both unexpected and inevitable.

At Co–Star, the materials are a 4,000-year-old system of astrology, planetary data from NASA, and a corpus written by astrologers and poets. The qualities we're designing for: astrology made accessible without asking anyone to learn a complex system, and a language that lets people share something intimate with their friends.

We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to continue cultivating those qualities across Co–Star and new experiments. You'll move between product architecture, interaction design, prototyping, and visual design. Ideas rarely arrive as polished specs. You'll help decide what we make next and how it works.

Jukebox is a fast-growing women’s personal care brand within the Dr. Squatch portfolio, redefining the category with bold, vibrant products made from natural, high-performance ingredients. - Concept and develop innovative design solutions across packaging, retail, digital, and print touchpoints — applying strong hierarchy, systems thinking, typography, and bold visual storytelling.

Wealth management is a $545 billion industry that still runs on manual work. 75% of advisors offer no digital communication beyond email, and most still build financial plans by hand in Excel. Savvy is reinventing what it looks like to be a financial advisor. Founder Ritik Malhotra saw the fragmentation firsthand after seeking out his own advisor, and started Savvy to give independent advisors a modern, AI-native home.

Savvy is a registered investment advisor (RIA), and we partner with experienced financial advisors who want to grow without running the back office themselves. Advisors bring their book and join Savvy, running under their own brand (or ours), and Savvy earns a percentage of the assets they manage. In return, they get a true business-in-a-box: a proprietary tech platform and client portal, an in-house marketing team that helps them grow, a world-class investment management team, and a dedicated client services team that runs day-to-day operations and support. Advisors at Savvy service up to 50% more households and save 19 hours a week.

Internally, everyone at Savvy uses Claude and is encouraged to experiment with it, backed by a dedicated AI enablement team and a RevOps org building agents in-house.

We're a Series B company hitting our stride, with roughly 150 employees and over 500% year-over-year growth, backed by $105M from Thrive Capital, Index Ventures, Canvas Ventures, and Mark Casady (former CEO of LPL Financial). Come help us scale!

Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. The system must handle multi-step reasoning, interact with external tools, and remain reliable despite non-deterministic model behavior. Our objective is to help users complete tasks daily enjoyable with over ~90%* reduced time.


Role
You will own the UX of A1's core app experience. This means designing the end-to-end flows users go through every day - how they start tasks, how they follow along as the AI works, how they stay in control, and how they recover when something goes wrong.

- Experience conducting user research and turning findings into design decisions.
- Comfortable working in fast-moving teams with evolving product scope.

description:

About SigmaMD


SigmaMD is changing the way people manage their health. We build the platform where modern clinics run their entire business on — clinician apps, patient apps, and the admin tooling behind them — covering charting, a number of embedded AI tools, e-prescribing, labs, scheduling, patient messaging, and the money.

About this role


We're looking for a senior product designer who wants more than screens. You'll own the design of our most demanding domain end to end — the research, the flows, the interface, and a real share of the product thinking behind it.


Your primary surface is Payments & Billing. Today our practices bill patients and employers directly: memberships and plan cycles, employer contracts with coverage rules, eligibility roster feeds, proration, invoices and charge items, refunds and reissues, superbills, and card/ACH processing through our merchant partner.


This is not a domain you can design from a wireframe kit. When a patient joins on the 14th, when an employer covers 60% up to a cap, when a membership pauses mid-cycle and is reinstated — someone has to understand exactly what the numbers do, then design an interface that makes it obvious to a physician who is not an accountant. About 9amHealth

9amHealth is an AI-enabled virtual specialty care platform focused on managing high-cost chronic conditions at scale. The company partners with employers, health plans, and pharmacy benefit managers to deliver comprehensive, cost-effective medical care for individuals living with obesity, diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. Members receive access to specialized clinicians, including endocrinologists, obesity medicine specialists, and clinical pharmacists, at-home lab testing, prescription medications, and lifestyle support.

9amHealth was founded in 2021 and is backed by leading healthcare investors like Define Ventures, SemperVirens, 7Wire Ventures, and The Cigna Group Ventures.

About The Role

We’re hiring a Senior Product Designer to own 9amHealth’s consumer app — the daily touchpoint for people managing diabetes, blood pressure, cholesterol, or weight. This is a craft-led, senior IC role. You’ll design what our members see, what they tap, and how the experience responds. The quality of what you ship matters as much as the thinking behind it.

The mandate is broad and the canvas is genuinely open. Several tracks in the 9amHealth member experience are still largely untouched: mental health support, movement, and more. You’ll put your fingerprint on labs, medications, virtual visits, education, nutrition, tracking, and the onboarding and re-engagement patterns that tie them together. For an ambitious senior designer who wants to shape a product from the ground up, that scope is rare.

Our members carry real clinical risk,including vulnerability to disordered eating patterns. That means no unnecessary pressure, no calorie scolding, no shame loops. Holding “engaging” and “clinically safe” in tension at the same time is the real design challenge here, and the thing that makes this role genuinely hard and genuinely interesting. It’s also the part that no tool can do for you,it requires judgment.

The member app is also tightly integrated with our EMR, which we built ourselves. Clinical data surfaces on the consumer side. Member actions trigger Care Team workflows. A “message your Care Team” button has a queue behind it. A surfaced lab value is the tip of a workflow. You’ll work primarily on the consumer surface, but you need to think across that seam, because your decisions shape the clinical team’s day.

This is a senior individual contributor role reporting to our Head of Design. You’ll work day-to-day with a full product squad: a product manager, front-end and back-end engineers, and QA. Our product and engineering team is distributed across San Diego, (CA) and Vienna (AU), and this role is based in EST for maximum overlap with both.

About Co-Star

Someone downloads Co–Star every 5 seconds.

In the five years since we launched, 25% of young people 18-25 in the US have downloaded the app. Big Sean has rapped about us, Ariana Grande & Kevin Durant post screenshots to their IGs, and we've been App of the Day twice. We don't pay for marketing – we designed the app to go viral, and it did.

Astrology has been popular for 4,000 years.

Astrology is a tool for speaking about yourself, about who you are, what you're experiencing, and how you relate to other people – in other words, a language for the things that really matter. It's a structured system, based on the physical locations of the planets in the sky, developed over millennia 4,000 years of practice.

Everyone has memories of reading a horoscope in the newspaper. You know your sign the same way you know the name of the street you grew up on. An average of 43% of Americans have believed in astrology since the 1970s.

We're merging the resonance of the humanities with the precision of technology.

Every word of it is based on each person's unique astrology: where the stars physically were when they were born and where those same stars are now. Co–Star combines the art of ancient practice with cutting-edge artificial intelligence, creating the first synthetic text to be called "wildly beautiful."

We're a small, experienced team.

title: Eyewear Designer
description:
At Pair Eyewear, we believe in placing our people at the center of everything we do. We are dedicated to fostering a joyful and dynamic workplace, providing our employees with an environment where they can thrive and make a meaningful impact.


Pair Eyewear is looking for a frame designer to own the look, feel, and design identity of our eyewear. This is a creative, concept-driven role: you’ll define the aesthetic direction of our frames and bring new shapes and collections to life through sketching, illustration, and hand-drawing. You’ll set the design vision and partner with our development team to take concepts toward production. If you have an eye for form, a point of view on style, and a love of eyewear, we want to see your work.


What You’ll Do:

- Define the look, feel, and design identity of Pair’s frames — from overall aesthetic direction to the details of each shape.
- Conceptualize and develop new frame designs through sketching, illustration, hand-drawing, and digital rendering.
- Explore form, proportion, silhouette, and style across the collection.
- Direct materials, color, and finish (CMF) — selecting and combining acetate, metal, and mixed materials to express each design.
- Develop balanced, on-trend collections aligned with the Pair brand and the product roadmap.
- Partner with the product development team to carry concepts from idea toward production, keeping the design intent intact.
- Research eyewear, fashion, and materials trends, and study competitor product, to keep the line fresh and distinct.
- Present design concepts and direction clearly to cross-functional partners.


Who You Are:

- A frame designer with a strong point of view on style, form, and what makes eyewear feel special.
- A skilled illustrator — confident in hand-drawing and digital sketching to communicate ideas quickly and beautifully.
- Trend-aware and curious, with a feel for where eyewear and fashion are heading.
- Organized and self-driven, able to run multiple designs in parallel against a product calendar.
- Collaborative — you enjoy working with development, category, and brand partners to bring designs to life.


Need to Have:

- Direct eyewear industry experience designing frames.
- Degree in Industrial Design, Product Design, Fashion Design, or a related field — design school strongly preferred. Equivalent professional experience considered.
- Strong hand-drawing, illustration, and digital sketching skills (e.g. Procreate, Photoshop, Illustrator).
- A strong sense of form, proportion, brand aesthetic, and color/material/finish.
- Working knowledge of eyewear materials and construction — enough to design with manufacturability in mind.
- A portfolio showing original eyewear / frame design, from concept through finished product.


Nice to Have:

- Experience designing for a direct-to-consumer/ wholesale retail or high-volume eyewear brand.
- Specialized eyewear-design training or apprenticeships.
- A background in trend or CMF research.

You will participate in a remote session to review various design artifacts and provide structured feedback. We're looking for a Design Lead to help lead that effort.

You'll partner closely with our Chief Design Officer to shape the future of Midjourney's products while building and leading the product design team.

This isn't a traditional management role. You’ll spend meaningful time designing, prototyping, reviewing work, and solving difficult product problems alongside your team. Most days you will be helping exceptional designers do the best work of their careers by building with them. If your favorite part of leadership is modeling what good looks like by collaborating and getting your hands dirty with your team, you’ll probably enjoy it here.

- Work closely with the Chief Design Officer to shape the direction of Midjourney's products. 
- Recruit, mentor, and lead the product design team. 
- Stay close to the work by designing key product experiences and helping teams solve their hardest design problems. 
- Partner closely with engineering and research to turn new tech into intuitive product experiences. 
- Establish design reviews and operating rhythms that help the team do its best work. 
- Ensure a coherent experience across Midjourney's growing portfolio of products. 

You might be a fit if



- You've spent the last decade designing software people love to use. 
- You've led design teams, but you still want to be in Figma every day. 
- You're as comfortable thinking through product strategy as you are refining a single interaction. 
- You work well with engineers and like building things that don't have established playbooks. 
- You care about craft and iterate until something feels right. 
- You're comfortable using tools like Claude Code and Cursor as part of your workflow. 
- You believe the best work comes from showing work early and often, and collaboratively iterating on unfinished work
- You're excited by the idea that AI requires entirely new interaction paradigms, not just new features. 
- Work > ego
- Prototypes > presentations

Logistics



- Full-time. San Francisco Hybrid. 
- Compensation: $285,000–$350,000 + benefits

To apply

A portfolio is required.

We care much more about what you've made than where you've worked. If this role excites you, we'd love to hear from you—even if you don't check every box.

At DICK’S Sporting Goods, we believe in how positively sports can change lives. On our team, everyone plays a critical role in creating confidence and excitement by personally equipping all athletes to achieve their dreams. We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workforce, reflecting the communities we serve.

If you are ready to make a difference as part of the world’s greatest sports team, apply to join our team today!

Overview

The Designer is responsible for the entire design process for a specific apparel category or brand within the DICK’s Sporting Goods portfolio of vertical brands. This includes completing global market research to identify trends and innovation, trend board creation, designing, sketching, tech packs and establishing expression of fit. The Designer must identify the needs of his/her target athlete and develop a product vision that aligns to these needs. Through the design of the upcoming seasonal product assortment, the Designer must bring his/her vision to life.

CALIA is a women's fitness & lifestyle apparel brand sold exclusively at DICK's Sporting Goods. All CALIA products are designed to be equal parts feminine & functional using premium materials that are sophisticated and stay on trend without being trendy. CALIA is designed for women who lead an active lifestyle & need a versatile wardrobe to take them through their day. The ideal candidate for this role has an eye for fashion and trend, demonstrates curiosity, a can-do attitude and can adapt to a fast paced environment.

Manage And Drive The Design Process



- Own the seasonal line direction from concept to production for all product and assortment needs by owning the design and development process, leading the creation of product and driving the creative direction by executing innovative design solutions, incorporating technology, color, fabric/finish standards, print and pattern, trim and expression of fit for multiple products/genders/demographic based on category.
- Develop silhouette and product classifications, within the framework of the assortment plan, to reflect a balance between fashion/trend as well as core and emerging businesses for presentation to and selection by the Merchant and Product Development team.
- Responsible for the accurate and timely completion of tech pack creation and handoff to tech designers; coordinates the design and development process for multiple products/categories from concept sketches and technical packs through final prototype/adoption.
- Attend seasonal fit analysis and weekly fit sessions to drive the expression of fit for multiple brands. Work in partnership with the fabric specialist to achieve costing and aesthetic goals for the seasonal fabric palette. 
- Communicate with overseas partners on trends, details and communicates any required changes to ensure the design vision for the brand is met. 
- Present during seasonal line review with Leadership across Product Development and Merchand

title: Freelance B2B eCommerce CRO & Product Designer
description:

Our mission is to help customers save time and money when purchasing commercial kitchen equipment and supplies by providing a customer-centric shopping experience and leveraging our industry buying power.

title: Graphic Designer
description:
Graphic Designer


We're looking for a talented Graphic Designer with a strong foundation in visual design and a passion for creating exceptional print materials. This role is ideal for a designer who understands that great design starts with typography, composition, color, and attention to detail—not just software proficiency. 


While print design will be your primary focus, you'll also contribute to digital marketing and social media projects, helping ensure our brand is consistent across all channels.


Responsibilities



- Design high-quality print materials including signage, point-of-sale materials, advertisements, and promotional pieces.
- Apply strong typography, layout, color, and visual hierarchy to every project.
- Prepare production-ready files and perform various production related tasks.
- Maintain and evolve brand standards across print and digital applications.
- Design digital assets for websites, email marketing, online advertising, and social media.
- Collaborate with marketing and cross-functional teams to develop creative concepts from idea to execution.
- Manage multiple projects while meeting deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

- Bachelor's degree in Graphic Design or related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Exceptional typography, layout, composition, and color skills.
- Extensive experience designing for print and preparing files for production.
- Advanced skills in Adobe Creative Cloud, especially InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop.
- Experience creating graphics for social media and digital marketing campaigns.
- Strong understanding of branding and visual identity systems.
- Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills.
- Ability to receive feedback, communicate design decisions, and work collaboratively.
What We're Looking For


We're seeking someone who is a team player, values craftsmanship and believes that successful design is built on strong fundamentals. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable refining the smallest typographic detail in a print piece as they are creating engaging graphics for various media. If you're passionate about thoughtful, well-executed design and take pride in producing work but not afraid to perform heavy production tasks, we'd love to hear from you.

Guided by its mission to Make People and Nature Healthier Through Biotechnology, and its role as a well-recognized biotechnology company, GenScript has a team of approximately 6,165 employees and has served more than 200,000 customers across over 100 countries and regions. 
Job Title: Senior Product Designer / Senior Strategic Product Manager (Life Science Reagents)
Position Type: Full-time, Strategic/Front-end Portfolio Management
Location: Piscataway, New Jersey
Compensation: The estimated salary range is $125,000 - $155,000 based upon experience level.
Job Scope:
At GenScript, we believe great products begin long before the first experiment. As a Senior Product Designer under GenScript's Catalog Products Business Unit, you won't simply manage existing products—you will design the future of our life science research portfolio.
This role sits at the intersection of science, technology, customer insight, and business strategy, helping define WHAT products GenScript should build over the next 3–5 years. Focused purely on front-end strategic planning, you will define the target specifications (What) while liberating R&D to explore the best execution (How).
You will work closely with R&D, Marketing, Business Development, Commercial, and executive leadership to discover unmet customer needs, identify emerging technology opportunities, design high-barrier product portfolios, and shape long-term innovation strategy.
Key Responsibilities (What You'll Do):
1) Design Future Product Portfolio & Roadmaps

- Portfolio Strategy: Build long-term product portfolio strategies across antibodies, recombinant proteins, enzymes, bioassays, protein purification products, Cell & Gene Therapy (GCT) reagents, and emerging technology platforms.
- White Space Identification: Pinpoint technology white spaces and unarticulated customer needs to establish a sustainable, high-margin product menu.
- Strategic Roadmapping: Formulate and maintain future product roadmaps aligned with global business unit growth objectives.
2) Customer Insights & Actionable VOC

- Deep Workflow Understanding: Transform scientific insights into commercial opportunities by deep-diving into customer workflows, Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD), and Voice of the Customer (VOC).
- Market Intuition: Keep a pulse on emerging research trends, technology evolution, and the global competitive landscape. Your goal is to discover latent opportunities that customers have not yet articulated.
3) Shape Innovation & Platform Strategy

- Multidimensional Evaluation: Evaluate future portfolio opportunities by integrating scientific feasibility, customer value, market potential, competitive differentiation, intellectual property (IP), and business economics.
